business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Absorbable Polyglycolic Acid Braided Sutures

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Colombia (national jurisdiction, no separate provincial corporate registries)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic) with unitary administrative structure
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 2012)
Colombia-Spain Bilateral Investment Treaty (1995) and Double Taxation Agreement (in force 2008)
Colombia-Chile, Colombia-Mexico (Pacific Alliance) Framework Agreements on trade and investment

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 2010 of 2019 (as amended); Decree 1529 of 2021 (UBO definition and threshold); Articles 631-1 and 631-2 of the Colombian Tax Statute; Law 1121 of 2006 (AML/CFT); Decree 1068 of 2015 (regulating the Financial Information and Analysis Unit - UIAF); Law 1762 of 2015 (extortion and money-laundering offence); Superintendency of Companies Resolution 202-01-002461 of 2021 (UBO register for supervised companies); DIAN regulations on Beneficiario Final annual reporting.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Corporate Existence and Representation (Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal) of the foreign corporate parent or subscriber
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry / Chamber of Commerce in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the country of origin, or consular legalization where the origin state is not party to the Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special Power of Attorney (Poder Especial) appointing the local Colombian attorney-in-fact or incorporator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or notarial office of the shareholder/board in the source jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (preferred) or consular legalization by the Colombian Consulate if the source state is outside the Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Constitutional Charter, By-laws and amendments of the foreign parent company, together with a director's certificate of authority to incorporate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry and authorized director/administrator of the foreign entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; in non-Apostille states, Colombian consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified or notarized copy of the shareholder/director's identification (passport or national ID)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or notary public of the shareholder's residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for registered ID copies; Colombian consular legalization for foreign unregistered private documents from non-Apostille countries

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening under Law 1121/2006, Law 2010/2019 and UIAF guidelines. Each direct and indirect shareholder, beneficial owner, and legal representative is screened against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council consolidated list, EU/UK financial sanctions lists, Colombian National Registry of Persons Sanctioned for Money-Laundering, and the official Colombian government PEP database (Libro SIREL). Enhanced due diligence is required for non-resident sovereign investors, PEPs, and clients using Swift_LC or TT_Wire payment rails. Autonomous review of the UBO register threshold is performed at 5% ownership or control.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RUES - Registro Único Empresarial y Social (www.rue.com.co), operated by the Chamber of Commerce network; name availability search is performed in the alpha-name system of the relevant Chamber, e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (www.ccb.org.co)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Spanish-compatible Latin script. The final name must include the suffix 'S.A.S.' Transliteration from foreign scripts is acceptable if rendered phonetically in standard Spanish letters (A-Z, Ñ, Ü). Names in English or other languages are allowed only when transliterated and do not conflict with Spanish syntax requirements.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco (bank) - prior approval of Superintendencia Financiera
Seguros / Aseguradora (insurance) - prior approval of Superintendencia Financiera
Cooperativa - prior registration with Superintendencia de la Economía Solidaria
Universidad / Colegio - prior approval of Ministry of Education
Hospital / Clínica / Salud - prior approval of Ministry of Health and Social Protection
Servicio Público / Empresa de Servicios Públicos - prior legal authorization
Minera / Petróleo / Carbón - prior approval of Ministry of Mines and Energy
Policía / Fuerzas Militares / Defensa - prior approval of Ministry of Defense
Nacional / Estado / Oficial - restricted to public entities or concessionaires
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended once for an additional 30 calendar days by filing before the same Chamber of Commerce before expiry. Upon rejection, the applicant may submit a written recurso de reposición within ten (10) working days before the same Chamber requesting reversal. If the Chamber maintains the refusal, the applicant may invoke the administrative appeal regime of Law 1437 of 2011 or, alternatively, request a judicial determination before the competent civil court through the special proceedings for company law matters under the Colombian Commercial Code.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for the registered administrative office and notification address for the S.A.S., including in the RUES, as long as a physical operating address exists where the medical-device and suture assembly activity is conducted. For this ISIC 3250 activity, the manufacturing facility will require its own physical address and enforcement-relevant infrastructure under Decree 4725 of 2005 (health registry and INVIMA surveillance). A 'virtual office alone' is not sufficient to satisfy commercial substance for a manufacturing business.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 30% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the Chamber of Commerce within the first 18 months if a virtual office is declared. The rate rises to 40% when INVIMA regulatory inspections for medical devices are included. With a dedicated, staffed registered office and compliant manufacturing site, the expected annual inspection probability is reduced to approximately 10% for the registry and 20% for INVIMA in the first two years.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External counsel, tax accountant, or compliance consultant

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008, Articles 1–50 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada); applicable provisions of Código de Comercio (Decree 410 of 1971) on commercial registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (Chamber of Commerce of the registered office jurisdiction) and Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation document) – registered with the Cámara de Comercio; a public deed is required if real property capital contributions are made.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Colombian S.A.S., but capital must be fully subscribed and may be paid in installments per the bylaws; shares must be issued for monetary instruments, in-kind assets, or intellectual property. No escrow account is legally mandated for capital formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Shareholders, representing one hundred percent of the subscribed capital, unanimously resolve: (1) to approve the issuance and subscription of the founder shares, with the capital contribution schedule set forth in the bylaws; (2) to adopt as the registered office the address identified in the formation dossier, declaring it the principal place of business and domicile for all legal notices; (3) to appoint the undersigned individuals as legal representative, alternate legal representative, and statutory auditor, respectively, each to serve until the following ordinary shareholders’ meeting; and (4) to instruct the legal representative to execute all ancillary filings, registrations, and permits necessary to commence lawful operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio / RUES online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search request to the local Chamber of Commerce via the RUES portal to obtain a non-commercial-name conflict certificate. Provide up to five alternative proposed names. The system will issue a 'Certificado de Homonimia' confirming the name is available for registration.
required_dossiers: Completed name availability request form
Proposed company name (up to five choices)
Identity document of the requesting shareholder or legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as too similar to an existing registration, file a written substitution request with the Chamber of Commerce proposing a new name or a clear morphological differentiation; pay the nominal re-filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (if public deed required) and/or shareholders' meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Documento Privado de Constitución in accordance with Ley 1258. Include corporate purpose (ISIC 3250 – manufacture of surgical sutures and needles), agreed capital, share classes, governance provisions, fiscal year, and dispute resolution clause. All subscribing shareholders must sign the document before a notary for authentication if real estate is contributed; otherwise, private signatures suffice. If public deed is required, register the deed with the corresponding notary.
required_dossiers: Final draft of the incorporation document/bylaws
Acceptance letters of appointed legal representative, alternate, and statutory auditor
Copy of shareholders' identity documents
Notarized powers of attorney (if shareholders act through representatives)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any missing statutory clause or signature as flagged by the notary or Chamber; resubmit the amended document. For notarial objections, coordinate with the notary to obtain a certified correction and reconvene the shareholders if substantive governance terms are amended.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the company with the Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed incorporation document and ancillary forms with the Chamber of Commerce in the municipality where the registered office is established. Complete the RUES pre-registration form, pay the registration fee, and obtain the certificate of incorporation and commercial registry (Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal).
required_dossiers: Executed incorporation document (private document or notarial deed)
Certificate of name availability (Certificado de Homonimia)
RUES pre-registration shipment
Payment receipt for stamp taxes and registration fee
Identification documents of shareholders and legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, cure by submitting missing corporate data (e.g., exact share capital amounts, domicile) within the Chamber’s prescribed 10-day correction window. Failure to cure results in rejection; file a new application with full corrected data after paying the fee again.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for national tax ID (NIT) with DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN – Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Chamber-issued certificate, request the NIT via DIAN’s online portal or regional office. Complete RUT (Registro Único Tributario) with the company’s address and legal representative’s information. Obtain the RUT with the final NIT, marking the company as responsible for corporate income tax, VAT, and industry and commerce tax if applicable.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal (issued by Chamber of Commerce)
Identification and RUT of the legal representative
Corporate email and contact details
Completed RUT form (Formulario 002)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUT is rejected for inconsistencies, correct the data via the DIAN portal and re-submit. For unresolved data inconsistencies, schedule a DIAN assistance appointment or submit a formal correction petition (derecho de petición).

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banking entity (subject to Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Choose a regulated bank and present the incorporation certificate, NIT is required? (The NIT is issued after NIT registration; bank account opening requires the RUT). Present the corporate legalization documents to open a checking and/or escrow account. Confirm whether the capital contribution will be deposited; for an S.A.S., deposits are not legally required unless agreed, but the bank requires initial deposit for account maintenance.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal (no older than 90 days)
NIT/RUT certificates
Bylaws and initial board resolution designating each account's authorized signatories
Identity documents of all authorized signatories
Proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes enhanced due diligence due to the medical device manufacturing classification, provide a certified description of the regulated activities and any pre-approval from INVIMA to accelerate the account opening. Alternatively, submit written clarification to the bank's compliance officer (Oficial de Cumplimiento) and obtain a formal decision within 15 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register commercial books and bookkeeping records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio (via RUES) for registration of accounting books
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, register the company's official accounting books (libro de actas, libro de accionistas, and accounting records) with the Chamber of Commerce. This is done through the 'Registro de Libros' service, either physically or electronically, within two months of company formation. For each book, submit the first opening page to be sealed by the Chamber.
required_dossiers: Registration application for commercial books
Incorporation certificate (Certificado de Existencia)
Book preparation evidence (journal, ledger, minutes book, and shareholder registry)
Payment of registration fee per book
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the books are rejected due to missing seals or incorrect format, correct the books in accordance with the Chamber’s technical guide and resubmit within 30 days; pay the applicable late fee if the initial two-month period has elapsed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: INVIMA – Instituto Nacional de Vigilancia de Medicamentos y Alimentos (and for sanitary licensing, the municipal or departmental health secretariat under Decree 4725/2005)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro Sanitario de Dispositivo Médico (Sanitary Registry of Medical Device) and Certificate of Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) for the assembly and packaging of surgical sutures and needles

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: ANLA – Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (or the regional Corporación Autónoma Regional if the project is within local jurisdiction)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 – Moderate Impact Specific Environmental Permit (Permiso Ambiental Sectorial); a full EIA report is not mandatory for small-scale sutures assembly, but environmental compliance registration with annual environmental performance reporting is required under Resolution 1408/2015.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For wastewater discharges: comply with Decree 3930/2010 as amended by Resolution 631/2015 – minimum thresholds: pH 6.0–8.5, COD ≤ 200 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 100 mg/L, total suspended solids ≤ 80 mg/L, and maximum oil/grease ≤ 10 mg/L. For industrial process air emissions (if soldering or needle sterilizing apertures): apply volatile organic compound (VOC) concentration ≤ 60 mg/m³ per source, odor concentration below the emission limit under Resolution 909/2008, and particulate matter ≤ 50 mg/m³. Hazardous waste must be managed under Resolution 1181/2006 and disposed only through licensed carriers.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos (issued after inspection for fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and evacuation plans); structural load inspection issued by the local curator's office or registered engineer confirming machine and mezzanine loads; workplace safety clearance from the ARL (Administradora de Riesgos Laborales) confirming compliance with the company's occupational health and safety management system (SG-SST) under Decree 1072/2015.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) - National Directorate of Taxes and Customs; official portal: www.dian.gov.co (DIAN Virtual Office / MUISCA transactional platform for tax registration, filing, electronic invoicing, and customs declarations).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Colombian S.A.S. must enroll with DIAN through the MUISCA Virtual Office by submitting the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) application, which automatically assigns the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) as the statutory tax identifier. The legal representative must hold a Colombian tax ID (NIT or citizenship card) and digitally sign the enrollment. The RUT must record the principal and secondary CIIU economic activity codes (with code 3250 for surgical instrument and suture manufacture), IVA responsible-entity status (Responsable de IVA - Régimen Común), exporter status (Exportador) for zero-rated operations, and the authorized electronic invoicing resolution. Foreign shareholders may incorporate remotely; if the S.A.S. has no local physical establishment, a local agent or domicile address is required for DIAN notifications. The NIT must appear on all income tax returns, VAT returns, withholding certificates, electronic invoices, and export declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - the Colombian S.A.S. is a distinct resident corporate taxpayer subject to entity-level corporate income tax under a worldwide income principle (renta mundial), with foreign tax credits for eligible foreign-source taxes; no pass-through or partnership look-through applies to an S.A.S. for income tax purposes. Territorial_Scope: resident entities are taxed on worldwide income, while non-resident recipients are taxed only on Colombian-source income. Tax_Exempt_Zone is not the default classification but is contractually available under Zona Franca legislation subject to DIAN approval and export/employment commitments.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia has no US-style check-the-box election and no elective hybrid-mismatch regimes; entity-level taxation is mandatory for an S.A.S. Available statutory elections relevant to an S.A.S. medical-device manufacturer: (i) registration as a Free Trade Zone user (Usuario Industrial de Bienes) under Law 1780/2016 and Decreto 2147/2016, contractually electing a 20% reduced CIT rate in exchange for export and employment commitments; (ii) optional consolidated tax group (consolidación fiscal) under E.T. Art. 19-1 for commonly controlled companies, elected before the fiscal year-end for a renewing three-year term; (iii) the simplified SIMPLE regime under Law 2010/2019 for small businesses, generally unavailable to exporters with CIIU 3250 above the SIMPLE size thresholds or activities subject to special regimes; and (iv) unilateral or bilateral Advance Pricing Agreements with DIAN for intercompany transactions. Anti-hybrid rules aligned with BEPS Action 2 disallow hybrid-mismatch deductions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre las Ventas) - value added tax (VAT/GST) levied on the sale, exchange, and import of goods and taxable services; supplemented by the Impuesto Nacional al Consumo (national consumption tax) applicable to select goods and services such as telecommunications, new vehicles, alcoholic beverages, and gaming services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis economic turnover threshold - every person or entity habitually selling taxable goods or services in Colombia must register with DIAN (RUT) as a responsible IVA party regardless of revenue level; even occasional importers need an NIT for customs clearance. Consequently, the S.A.S. must complete DIAN registration immediately upon incorporation and before any domestic sale, export, or import. Narrow exemptions apply only to isolated single transactions and not to recurring manufacturing operations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) governed by DIAN Resolution 000165 of 2023 (and prior Resolutions 000042/2020 and 000100/2021). All IVA responsible parties must issue invoices through either (i) DIAN's web-service habilitación or (ii) certified Proveedores Tecnológicos (PTE). Each invoice XML is validated by DIAN in real time and must contain the digital stamping code (CUFE for invoices; CUDE for credit/debit notes) and a machine-readable QR code. Fiscal validation is a precondition for the buyer's VAT credit deduction and for customs clearance of exports. Exporters must additionally submit electronic export declarations (DEX) through MUISCA/SIGLO XXI and, when applicable, prior registration in the Ventanilla Única de Comercio Exterior (VUCE).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under E.T. Art. 481, exports of goods are excluded from IVA (functionally zero-rated), and the exporter is entitled to full refund of input VAT embedded in production and distribution costs (saldo a favor claimed on the bimonthly IVA return and refunded by DIAN or credited against other tax liabilities). Eligibility requires: (i) the S.A.S. must be the legal seller of the exported surgical suture goods to a foreign buyer; (ii) the goods must physically depart Colombian customs territory, evidenced by an approved Declaración de Exportación (DEX); (iii) the export sale must be at arm's length at a commercial FOB value consistent with transfer pricing rules; (iv) export proceeds must be repatriated through the Colombian foreign-exchange market within the statutory deadline; and (v) compliance with INVIMA requirements, including valid sanitary registration and export endorsement for Class II-III medical devices.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación - DEX) legally approved by DIAN through MUISCA/SIGLO XXI
Commercial invoice and packing list matching the DEX, weights, and Incoterms
Original Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill (air) evidencing physical departure from Colombian territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign-exchange purchase certificate (Certificado de Reintegro de Divisas) issued by the Colombian commercial bank proving FX repatriation
INVIMA export health certificate and valid medical-device registration proof (when applicable)
Certificate of origin for preferential tariff treatment, where claimed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN, the Banco de la República, and Customs audit the full export triangle (invoice value, physical shipment, and FX reintegro), including input-VAT credit tracing to exported goods. Deficiencies trigger: (i) retroactive reversal of the export exclusion, recharacterization with 19% IVA assessed on the exporter, and denial of related input credits; (ii) sanction for improper VAT refund (devolución improcedente) up to 200% of the amount refunded under E.T. Art. 647, plus moratory interest; (iii) sanction for inaccuracy (sanción por inexactitud) of 100% of the excessive credit or understated liability under E.T. Art. 647-1; (iv) customs penalties and confiscation under Ley 1762/2015 contrabando provisions and Decreto 4747/2010; and (v) criminal liability of up to 9 years' imprisonment for fraudulent export declarations or unlawful FX under Código Penal Art. 337 and Ley 1762/2015. Overdue refunds improperly collected are clawed back with real-time interest from the date of payment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la Republica de Colombia (Central Bank of Colombia), acting through its Board of Directors (Junta Directiva) as the foreign-exchange regulatory authority, together with the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia for banking and AML/CFT supervision, and the Direccion de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales for trade and foreign-investment documentation controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia operates a managed floating exchange rate regime with a regulated foreign-exchange market (Mercado Cambiario). The Colombian peso is freely convertible through licensed Intermediarios del Mercado Cambiario (IMCs), principally commercial banks. Current-account transactions are fully convertible for trade in goods, services, royalties, and profit remittances, provided the underlying transaction is supported by the appropriate Declaracion de Cambio. Capital-account inflows, including foreign direct investment (FDI) and external credit, are lawful without prior authorization but must be registered with Banco de la Republica through an IMC within the applicable statutory declaration windows. Profit and dividend remittances to non-resident shareholders are permitted only where the originating foreign investment has been duly registered; unregistered capital cannot be repatriated. Capital outflows such as capital reductions, share disposals, and repayment of external debt are likewise conditioned on registration and on the satisfaction of Colombian withholding taxes. No dual exchange rate, no surrender requirement, and no pre-approval for trade-related FX operations apply; the practical impediments are documentary, comprising registration deadlines, exchange-declaration concept codes, and bank-level source-of-funds verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Goods exporters must repatriate (reintegrar) export proceeds through an IMC within six (6) months from the date of shipment, with Banco de la Republica empowered to grant extensions up to a maximum of fourteen (14) months on justified grounds. Service exporters must collect proceeds within four (4) months from the date of service provision, extendable up to twelve (12) months. Statutory mandatory conversion ratio into COP: 0%. Colombian law imposes no obligation to convert export receipts into pesos; the exporter may retain the foreign currency in a Banco de la Republica-registered foreign-currency compensation account (cuenta de compensacion) held with an IMC or elect to sell the currency at the market indicative rate (TRM). Notwithstanding the absence of conversion requirements, the entirety of each export receipt must be channeled through the foreign-exchange market and evidenced to the IMC by the Export Proceeds Exchange Declaration (Declaracion de Cambio - Form 1) supported by the Dian export registration. Expiry of the statutory collection period without reintegration constitutes an exchange-regime infraction subject to administrative penalties imposed under the Colombian foreign-exchange penalty regime.

Operational Current Account / Trade Finance Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: LOW as the principal treasury rail; MEDIUM for ancillary small-ticket receivables collection. Colombian SEDPEs (Sociedades Especializadas en Depositos y Pagos Electronicos) established under Law 1735 of 2014 are confined to domestic electronic deposits and payment wallets; they are not licenced IMCs and cannot open USD compensation accounts, execute foreign-investment registration, or issue the statutory exchange declarations required for capital injections and trade settlements. Unlicensed offshore EMIs and digital banks (for example Wise, Airwallex, Mercury, and Payoneer) are not authorized IMCs in Colombia; channelling Colombian-resident foreign-exchange transactions through them would breach the mandatory reintegro regime, compromise the SAS's ability to obtain timely Bank of Colombia registrations, and materially impair the domestic bank's KYC and source-of-funds attestation. Such EMIs may be used only as an auxiliary collection vehicle for low-value digital-service or R&D receivables, with subsequent onward transfer to the Colombian IMC compensation account, and must be disclosed to the primary relationship bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Definitive onboarding of a corporate account at a Colombian IMC will in principle require the verified physical or remote presence of the SAS's legal representative. Under Decree 2177 of 2017 and Article 11-3 of the Estatuto Organico del Sistema Financiero, Colombian banks are permitted to onboard clients through non-face-to-face identification using biometric verification and advanced electronic signature; in practice Bancolombia and Davivienda accept a remote video-identification interview for low-risk manufacturing companies, followed by the physical delivery by courier of the notarized board resolution, certified signatory powers, and original books. A foreign parent's directors are not required to travel to Colombia provided the resident legal representative attends the interview and holds a notarized and apostilled power of attorney; the domicile inspection of the registered office is customarily conducted by the bank's compliance team or a delegated third party. Documentary minimums include the SAS Registro Unico Tributario (RUT), Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation issued by the Camara de Comercio within the last 90 days, the notarized shareholders' resolution resolving account opening and signatory designation, and identification documentation of all beneficial owners holding five percent or more of capital or control.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: nominee shareholders or a multi-layer offshore holding structure above the Colombian SAS
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Camara de Comercio certificate of the SAS including the full shareholder register; notarized chain-of-title documentation of issued shares; sworn UBO declaration identifying every individual owner above the five-percent direct or indirect threshold in accordance with SFC Circular Basica Juridica 004/2022; corporate registry records for each intermediate legal entity; and a group ownership chart showing ultimate natural persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or AML list match on any signatory, director, or beneficial owner, including OFAC, UN, EU, and Colombian national lists
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent third-party screening reports (World-Check or equivalent) run at onboarding and refreshed quarterly; sworn declarations of non-PEP and non-sanctions status for each principal; adverse-media and name-similarity clarification letters with government-issued identification; and, where the foreign parent is US or Chinese-domiciled, the parent's certificate of good standing and a copy of its group sanctions-compliance policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector-regulatory mismatch: manufacture and export of surgical suture devices without Colombian sanitary and health-authority registrations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: INVIMA sanitary registration or pre-market permit covering the surgical suture needle assembly product line; ISO 13485 quality-management certificate for the manufacturing plant; Dian export regime certificate; process and product descriptions supporting the medical-device classification; and, where applicable, the free-sale certificate issued by INVIMA for each export destination.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party funding or intra-group loans injected as initial capital from the foreign parent without transparent source of funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed FDI contribution agreement or intra-group loan agreement; parent-company board resolution authorizing the remittance; remitter bank statement and transfer-valuation evidence; notarized SAS shareholders' minute approving the capital increase; and the Banco de la Republica foreign-investment registration (Form 4) or external-debt registration receipt filed through the IMC before the funds are deployed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume trade-payment pattern exhibiting pass-through characteristics, raising trade-based money laundering (TBML) concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade file per shipment: proforma invoice, final commercial invoice, bill of lading or airway bill, packing list, INVIMA export certificate, inspection certificate, and insurance certificate; quarterly reconciliation mapping each incoming SWIFT MT103 to a genuine export shipment; and the corresponding Declaraciones de Cambio settled with the IMC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic-connectivity indicator triggered by a foreign shareholder resident in a tax haven or non-cooperative jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Colombian substance evidence: lease agreements for the manufacturing premises, local payroll records, utility invoices, and fixed-asset purchase documents; OECD-aligned transfer-pricing documentation under Law 1819 of 2016; and the foreign shareholder's certificate of tax residence or a legal opinion explaining the substantive commercial rationale for the offshore structure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign investor remits USD via SWIFT MT103 (with MT202 cover where applicable) from its own account at a non-sanctioned, reputable bank to the beneficiary SAS account held with the Colombian IMC, earmarked as the foreign-investment sub-account. The MT103 field 72 (or designated purpose field) must state the payment concept: 'Foreign Direct Investment - capital contribution in foreign currency', and include the beneficiary's full legal name, NIT, address, and the underlying share-subscription reference. The IMC verifies the remitter against sanctions and PEP lists and issue the exchange-declaration receipt; the legal representative then submits the Foreign Investment Exchange Declaration (Form 4 of the Declaracion de Cambio) to Banco de la Republica through the IMC within the statutory filing window from the effective date of the investment, thereby obtaining the Registro de Inversion Internacional (RII). The proceeds may be monetized into COP at the TRM or credited to the company's USD compensation account. The SAS may not use the funds for operational outlays before the registration is perfected; any later dividend or capital repatriation is conditioned on a completed RII. If the injection is structured as debt rather than equity, the parent loan must be registered with Banco de la Republica as external credit under the external-debt regime, and any encaje (reserve requirement) then prevailing must be complied with by the borrowing SAS.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For open-account export receivables, the buyer's bank executes a SWIFT MT103 to the SAS USD compensation account at the Colombian IMC, quoting the commercial invoice number and the HS/INVIMA product reference, followed by the SAS submission of the Export Proceeds Exchange Declaration (Form 1). For documentary-credit sales, the Colombian IMC advises and settles the irrevocable letter of credit (SWIFT MT700 issuance by the buyer's bank, advice in MT710/MT720, amendment MT707); payment against compliant presentation of the commercial invoice, packing list, inspection certificate, INVIMA export certificate, insurance certificate, and transport document is effected via MT754/MT756 and covered by MT202, after which the export proceeds are declared on Form 1. For import disbursements of raw materials and components, the SAS instructs its IMC to execute outbound SWIFT MT103 (telegraphic-transfer payment) or, for recurring supply relationships, opens a commercial documentary credit locally through the IMC (MT700 issued by the Colombian bank), accompanied by the Dian import declaration and the corresponding Import Exchange Declaration (Form 1 for goods, Form 2 for services) within the stipulated declaration period. Every outbound wire must quote the underlying invoice or purchase-order number so the IMC can reconcile the transaction against the exchange-declaration record; repayment of intra-group foreign-currency loans must reference the external-debt registration number issued by Banco de la Republica.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/COP forward (forward de tasa de cambio) executed with the relationship IMC bank, limited to hedging the SAS's real commercial exposure arising from USD export receivables and USD-denominated imported-input payables, with tenors customarily up to 12 months.

USD/COP currency swap (swap de tasa de cambio) used for tenor-matched conversion and recharacterization of the SAS's USD operating cash flow into COP funding requirements, permissible where both legs settle through the IMC.

USD/COP option-based structures, principally zero-cost collars and capped forwards, permitted for non-speculative hedging of net open FX position, subject to the IMC's credit approval and supporting underlying trade documentation.

Non-deliverable USD/COP forward (NDF) allowed where settlement cannot involve physical delivery of pesos to a non-resident counterparty; the NDF's taxable gain or loss must be recognized in the SAS's income tax computation and reported for balance-of-payments statistics through the IMC.

Cross-currency interest rate swap (CCIRS) between USD floating and COP fixed rates used to hedge the interest and principal exposure of a registered external-credit facility, conditional upon full Banco de la Republica external-debt registration and hedged-effect documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of merchant registration (renovación de la matrícula mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (Chamber of Commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 31 March of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal accrues default interest (approximately 1.5% per month) and monetary fines; persistent non-renewal may lead to suspension of the commercial registration and eventual cancellation of the company's status in the business registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (estados financieros) approved by shareholders and deposited with the commercial registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders must approve financial statements within three months after fiscal year-end (i.e., by 31 March); deposition with the Chamber of Commerce must occur within one month after approval (i.e., normally by 30 April)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deposit can trigger administrative fines, impede issuance of good-standing certificates, and constitute grounds for commercial registry sanctions; repeated omission may affect the company's legal representation evidence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial owner report (reporte de beneficiarios finales – RUBF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 1 June and 31 October, or the specific filing window formally established by DIAN for the relevant tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or untimely filing may expose the company to penalties under Article 651 of the Colombian Tax Code, which can reach 1% of gross income or 15,000 UVT (whichever is higher), and may extend the statute of limitations for tax periods involved.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local industry and commerce tax declaration (impuesto de industria y comercio – ICA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Secretaría Distrital de Hacienda (Bogotá) or corresponding municipal tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually according to the municipal calendar, generally in April and May for the prior taxable year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment produces default interest and fines up to 10% of the tax assessed; persistent non-filing can result in preservation activities and temporary suspension of commercial permits.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada (S.A.S.) is exempt from designating a statutory auditor (Revisor Fiscal) unless, at the close of the prior fiscal year, total assets exceed 5,000 times the monthly minimum legal wage (5,000 SMMLV, approximately COP 7.1 billion or USD 1.7 million), gross revenues exceed 3,000 SMMLV (approximately COP 4.3 billion or USD 1.0 million), or the company employs more than 200 workers; when any threshold is met, an independent certified audit is mandatory.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as incorporated into Colombian law by Decree 2420 of 2015, with subsequent amendments; companies classified in Grupo 1 apply full IFRS, Grupo 2 companies apply IFRS for SMEs (IFRS para las Pymes), and Grupo 3 micro-entities apply the simplified micro-entity standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual RUBF confirmation must be filed with DIAN during the statutory window and must reflect the ultimate beneficial owners as of 31 December of the preceding fiscal year; any share transfer or any change in beneficial ownership must be contemporaneously recorded in the company's shareholder register and subsequently reported in the next annual RUBF filing, with failure to do so subject to tax information penalties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders and Board Meetings
Share Transfer and Beneficial Owner Log

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% (general corporate income tax rate under Colombian Tax Code as amended by Law 2277 of 2022)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general corporate income tax holiday applies. Available preferential mechanisms include: 50% deduction for investments in real productive fixed assets; deduction for new employment generated in defined vulnerable/under-28 age groups; tax discount for investments in qualified science, technology, and innovation (CTeI) projects; and accelerated depreciation allowances. These are elective and must be substantiated in the annual income tax return and underlying schedules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 220 (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios para Personas Jurídicas) filed through DIAN's mandatory electronic filing platform MUISCA (Módulo de Usuario para Servicios y Cumplimiento Tributario)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (single final income tax return per fiscal year; prepayments are satisfied via required advance installments and periodic withholding remittances during the year)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year taxpayer, the return is due in the following tax year on the date assigned by the DIAN filing calendar, generally between 9 April and 20 April, depending on the last two digits of the taxpayer's NIT; non-calendar-year taxpayers file no later than the deadline prescribed by the DIAN calendar for the close of their approved fiscal year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification number and DIAN check digit; legal company name and fiscal address appear in the electronic header.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Colombian NIT of the S.A.S. itself. A non-resident shareholder may act as legal representative through a registered local agent but cannot substitute its own foreign tax identification number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year covered by the return, normally the calendar year ending 31 December.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A S.A.S. with non-resident ownership is not permitted to choose a non-calendar year without prior DIAN authorization; any approved short period must be shown and reconciled with the final liquidation of the prior period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate gross operating revenue, non-operating revenue, occasional gains, and restitution amounts. Export sales of surgical suture needle assemblies are included at invoice value converted to COP at the applicable DIAN exchange rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All Colombian-source income must be reported. Foreign parent purchasing the assembled sutures does not make the income foreign-source; the manufacturing and assembly are performed physically in Colombia and are fully taxable unless a specific export exemption applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income minus allowable costs, deductible expenses, provisions, amortization, and compensated tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions must be economically related to Colombian-source production. Payments to foreign related parties for raw material purchases, royalties, or technical services require transfer-pricing documentation and must meet arm's length standards; otherwise deductions may be disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computed by applying the 35% corporate rate to net taxable income, adding any special rates on occasional gains or untaxed dividend distributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty withholding reductions do not change the corporate-level tax; the 35% rate applies to the Colombian S.A.S., while any treaty benefits only affect distributions to foreign shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 24 - Tax Credits, Withholdings, and Prepayments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Creditable source withholdings, legally authorized tax discounts (CTeI, fixed-asset investment), and prior prepayments applied against the assessed tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are not automatically claimable unless the corresponding foreign-source income is included in the Colombian taxable base and a valid DTA credit provision applies. Retain certificates and wire/SWIFT records for audit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty equals 5% of the tax payable for each month or fraction of month of delay, up to a maximum of 100% of the tax; if no tax is payable, the penalty is 0.5% of gross income per month/fraction, capped at 100% of gross income. Default interest accrues daily at the DIAN tax rate. Delinquency also causes exclusion from government contracting benefits and may trigger criminal tax evasion proceedings if the return is false in substance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends paid from profits already subject to corporate income tax at the 35% rate; 20% on dividends paid from profits that were not taxed or were exempt. Treaty limits may reduce the rate (e.g., 0%, 5%, or 15% depending on the DTA and ownership percentage).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Double Tax Agreement, the non-resident beneficiary must submit to the Colombian paying entity before payment: (1) a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the beneficiary's tax authority, apostilled/legalized as required; (2) a sworn statement of beneficial ownership; and (3) supporting legal documentation of shareholding. The payer then applies the reduced treaty withholding at source in the corresponding DIAN withholding return. If the source reduction is challenged, the payer must withhold at the statutory rate and the beneficiary may seek refund through the DIAN refund process with the same documentation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory gross-basis withholding: interest paid to foreign beneficiaries 15%; royalties for intellectual property and software exploitation 15%; technical assistance fees 10%. Under applicable Colombian tax treaties, interest may be reduced to 10% or 0% and royalties to 5% or 10%, depending on the treaty and beneficial ownership conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: For FY2024, mandatory Local File and Master File arise when gross income exceeds 135,000 UVT (approximately COP 6,353,775,000); mandatory Transfer Pricing Informative Return (Form 120) is required when gross income exceeds 45,000 UVT (approximately COP 2,117,925,000). Thresholds are updated annually by DIAN resolution based on the UVT.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not maintain a UAE-style standalone Economic Substance Regulations filing, but the DIAN applies the Tax Code anti-abuse rule and substance-over-form doctrine under Article 869 of the Colombian Tax Code. A S.A.S. engaged in surgical consumables manufacturing must maintain real operational substance in Colombia - physical factory, personnel, inventory, board decisions, and bank accounts - to defend its taxable presence, deduct costs, and avoid recharacterization of transactions as sham or lacking business purpose.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax Evasion / False Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting export revenue from surgical suture needle assembly, inflating production costs, submitting false purchase invoices, or deliberately omitting taxable non-operating income on Form 220.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative sanction of 100% of the omitted tax or false credit; default interest; exclusion from large-taxpayer privileges; criminal tax evasion carries imprisonment of 48 to 108 months and fines equal to the value of the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil applies: directors and legal representatives who sign fraudulent returns are jointly and severally liable for the tax debt and sanctions; civil restitution of assets and embargoes may be ordered; travel bans and preventive detention may be imposed in criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling finished sutures to a foreign related distributor below arm's length, paying excessive royalties or interest to a foreign parent, or failing to file the required Transfer Pricing Informative Return (Form 120) and supporting Local/Master Files.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may adjust taxable income to the arm's length result and charge the resulting tax plus default interest; failure to file transfer pricing documentation carries significant monetary penalties based on the value of the undocumented transactions; inaccurate filings attract an additional penalty of 5% of the transaction gross amount or the disallowed adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil applies: executive officers who decide on the controlled transaction are jointly liable for the assessment and penalties if they knowingly signed incorrect documentation; deliberate profit-shifting may trigger money-laundering exposure and personal criminal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Colombian S.A.S. as a mere invoicing conduit for surgical consumables without local assembly operations, operational management, qualified employees, physical premises, or meaningful decision-making; converting intercompany purchases into artificial deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may disregard the legal structure, recharacterize the operations as Colombian-source generation, deny all associated deductions, impose the 100% evasion penalty, and apply the integrity sanctions of Article 869; if the manufacturing license from INVIMA is not properly held or the facility does not exist, regulatory cancellation follows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil applies: shareholders and directors who benefit from the sham structure are personally liable for the recomputed tax, interest, and penalties; courts may seize personal assets and issue domestic/international travel prohibitions pending tax-fraud proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering / AML Breaches through Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using false SWIFT descriptions, over- or under-invoicing letters of credit, routing payments through shell intermediaries, or deliberately structuring international transfers to evade dividend withholding or banking controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering under Article 323 of the Colombian Criminal Code is punishable by 10 to 30 years of imprisonment and a fine of up to 50,000 current legal monthly minimum wages; proceeds are subject to forfeiture; banking relationships are terminated and the company is reported to the financial intelligence unit (UIAF).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil applies: directors who direct, approve, or benefit from illicit payment routing face individual criminal liability, travel bans, asset freezes, and possible extradition under mutual legal assistance agreements; compliance officers may be sanctioned independently for failing to implement AML controls.
